title: 第十章 又一顿打
content_zh:
从镇上回来，江砚的心思，活络了不少。

    “摹刻”那两个字，像一把钥匙，在他心里捅开了一道缝。他越发笃定，自己身上的秘密，绝不只是个无用的怪事。这世上既有卫家那样的人家，靠“凭空造物”的本事撑起了泼天的权势——那他手里这支笔，只要摸透了门道，就未必不能成为他翻身的本钱。

    可这都是远话。眼下，他得先熬过明天。

    明天，就是沈贵说的那个限期了。

    这两天，江砚一边照常干活、偷偷打熬身子，一边见缝插针地试那支笔。他试着平心静气地写，试着带着情绪狂涂，试着回想冰河里那股濒死的不甘……可任他怎么折腾，那点温热，再没出现过第二次。

    “到底差在哪……”夜里，他对着那团暗淡的墨迹，百思不得其解。

    他隐约觉得，自己离那个“门道”，就差一层窗户纸。可那层纸，怎么也捅不破。

    就是在这种焦灼里，限期没到，新的麻烦却先一步找上了门。

    那天傍晚，江砚干完活，揣着自己午间省下的、藏在怀里的小半个杂面饼子——那是他这几日好不容易，从牙缝里、从干活的间隙里，一点一点抠出来的口粮，他打算留着，明天应付那要命的一关时，垫垫肚子,好歹有点力气。

    他刚走到院门口，就被堵住了。

    江狗剩,带着那几个一起把他扔进冰河的小子，又凑齐了。

    自打落水那事，江狗剩心虚了两天，见江砚没声张，胆子又肥了起来。这会儿几个人吊儿郎当地拦在门口，一脸不怀好意。

    “站住。”江狗剩斜睨着他，“听说你今儿揣了吃的？拿出来，兄弟几个分分。”

    江砚的脸沉了下来。

    那半块饼,是他明天的本钱。

    “没有。”他护住怀里，往旁边让。

    “没有？”江狗剩冷笑，一个眼色递过去,几个小子立刻散开,把江砚团团围在中间，“搜！”

    江砚一把按住怀口，往后退，背抵上了冰冷的土墙。

    “江狗剩，”他盯着对方，一字一句，“前两天冰河里那事，我没说出去。这饼，你别动。”

    提起冰河，江狗剩脸上闪过一丝慌乱，可当着这么多人的面，他骑虎难下，反倒恼羞成怒：“放你娘的屁！谁、谁把你扔冰河了？血口喷人！”他色厉内荏地一挥手，“给我打！打到他把饼吐出来为止！”

    几个小子一拥而上。

    江砚拼了命地护住怀里的饼，可寡不敌众。拳脚雨点般落下来，砸在他还没养好的旧伤上，疼得他眼前阵阵发黑。有人去掰他护着饼的手，有人朝他腿弯踹，他一个站不稳,被掀翻在地。

    地上的雪混着泥，冰冷刺骨。

    一只脚,重重地踩在了他的手背上——那只攥着小半块饼、也攥着那截秃笔的手。

    “撒手！”江狗剩骑在他身上，去抢他怀里的东西。
content_en:
After returning from town, Jiang Yan's mind became much more active.

    The two words "imprint" were like a key, piercing a crack in his heart. He became more and more certain that the secret inside him was more than just a useless weird thing. In this world, there are people like the Wei family, who rely on their ability to "create things out of thin air" to support their overwhelming power - then the pen in his hand, as long as he knows the ropes, may not be able to turn him around.

    But these are all distant words. For now, he had to get through tomorrow.

    Tomorrow is the deadline that Shen Gui said.

    In the past two days, Jiang Yan worked as usual and secretly stretched himself while trying out the pen at every opportunity. He tried to write calmly, tried to write wildly with emotions, tried to recall the unwillingness to die in the glacier... But no matter how hard he tried, that warmth never appeared again.

    "What's the difference..." At night, he looked at the dim ink stain and was puzzled.

    He vaguely felt that he was only a layer of window paper away from that "doorway". But that layer of paper couldn't be pierced no matter what.

    It was in this anxiety that new troubles came to the door before the deadline came.

    That evening, after Jiang Yan finished his work, he took the small half of a mixed flour pancake that he had saved during the lunch and hid in his arms - it was the ration that he had dug out little by little from between his teeth and from the gaps in his work these past few days. He planned to keep it to cushion his stomach and give him some strength when he faced the fatal test tomorrow.

    As soon as he reached the entrance of the courtyard, he was blocked.

    Jiang Goucheng and the boys who threw him into the glacier gathered together again.

    Jiang Gouchang felt guilty for two days since he fell into the water. Seeing that Jiang Yan remained silent, he became bolder again. At this moment, several people were blocking the door carelessly, looking ill-intentioned.

    "Stop." Jiang Goucheng squinted at him, "I heard you brought some food today? Take it out and share it with your brothers."

    Jiang Yan's face darkened.

    That half piece of cake is his capital for tomorrow.

    "No." He protected his arms and stepped aside.

    "No?" Jiang Goucheng sneered, and with a wink, the boys immediately dispersed and surrounded Jiang Yan, "Search!"

    Jiang Yan held his arms tightly, stepped back, and pressed his back against the cold earth wall.

    "Jiang Goucheng," he stared at the other person, word by word, "I didn't tell anyone about what happened in the glacier two days ago. Don't touch this cake."

    At the mention of Binghe, a trace of panic flashed across Jiang Goucheng's face, but in front of so many people, he couldn't get off the tiger's back, so he became angry and said, "Fuck you! Who, who threw you into Binghe? You're spitting blood!" He waved his hand in a stern tone, "Hit him! Beat him until he spits out the cake!"

    Several boys rushed forward.

    Jiang Yan tried his best to protect the cake in his arms, but he was outnumbered. The fists and kicks fell like raindrops, hitting his old wounds that hadn't healed yet, and the pain made his eyes go black. Someone tried to break off his hand that was protecting the cake, and someone kicked him in the leg. He couldn't stand still and was knocked to the ground.

    The snow on the ground was mixed with mud, and it was bitingly cold.

    One foot stepped heavily on the back of his hand - the hand that was holding the small half piece of cake and the bald pen.

    "Let go!" Jiang Goucheng rode on him and grabbed the things in his arms.
